decision: build the first working slice of mailflow; the host-app connector is built separately in the host repo, switched off until configured
why: Anton asked to build it and merge to main for review tomorrow

decision: use Next 15.5, React 19.2, Prisma 6.19, zod 3, Tailwind 4 and Biome
why: Anton agreed to the stack; it matches the first host app, so the approved prototype UI carries over

decision: done means a scripted end-to-end run: host app reports a failed payment, mailflow sends mail through a real Listmonk into Mailpit, waits, asks the host, sends the reminder, and stops when payment succeeds
why: a falsifiable check on the real chain beats unit tests alone

decision: use Listmonk v6.2.0 transactional API with subscriber_mode external and one pass-through template whose body is .Tx.Data.html piped to Safe
why: external mode sends without making every recipient a Listmonk subscriber, so mailflow owns rendering and Listmonk only delivers

decision: pass the subject inside data instead of the subject field
why: Listmonk parses a subject containing double braces as a template, which would mangle merge text

decision: Listmonk returns 200 when it queues a message, not when it sends it, and returns no message id; mailflow records accepted-by-Listmonk, not delivered
why: honest status in run history

decision: show the unsubscribe link only when the host passes an unsubscribe_url; Listmonk transactional mail has no unsubscribe tag
why: payment emails are transactional, and a dead link is worse than none

decision: sent one email through real Listmonk v6.2.0 into Mailpit with external mode and the pass-through template
why: riskiest unknown first: if Listmonk could not deliver our own HTML, the whole design changes
evidence: dev/compose.yml; Mailpit showed HTML byte-identical and subject with double braces intact

decision: a run is a cursor into a flat map of steps built from the workflow tree, plus a due time; a snapshot of the workflow is stored on the run
why: one structure for every step kind, and editing a workflow can never strand a run that is halfway through

decision: at most one email per step: a delivery row is written before calling Listmonk, and a leftover pending row stops the run for a human instead of resending
why: a duplicate payment email is worse than a late one

decision: Prisma refused migrate reset when run by an agent; tests use migrate deploy into a separate test schema and truncate per test instead
why: did not bypass the safety guard; the non-destructive path is enough

decision: the concurrency test first passed even with the lease removed, because the three ticks never overlapped; made the fake Listmonk slow so they do
why: a test that cannot fail proves nothing

decision: scripts/mutate.sh breaks six rules one at a time (stop events, interrupted send, lease, HTML escaping, check branch, signature age) and all six are caught
why: proof the tests guard the rules that matter

decision: first e2e run showed every email a day late; cause was the script fixing simulated day 0 before the server booted, so runs created later were not yet due
why: checked the run history before touching the engine; the engine was right and the harness was wrong
evidence: scripts/e2e.ts t0 now set after events are posted

decision: end-to-end through real Listmonk into Mailpit with three people: alex never pays, sam pays on day 1 by event, kim pays by day 5 and only the host check knows
why: the falsifiable done-check from the frame
evidence: npx tsx scripts/e2e.ts: 16 of 16 checks pass

decision: admin pages live in an (admin) route group whose layout and every page call requireAdmin; mutations are server actions that call it again
why: one gate per surface, and a server action is a public endpoint so it can't rely on the page having checked

decision: the brand preview calls a server action that runs the real MJML renderer, debounced 250ms, instead of a client-side copy of the renderer
why: the preview can't drift from what recipients get

decision: 'where they are' is a pure function of status, cursor, dueAt and the run's definition snapshot
why: the engine moves the cursor past a wait and stores dueAt, so a future dueAt means waiting and the cursor is the next step; unit-tested

decision: Playwright walk against the e2e data: 19 checks incl. signed-out redirect, status toggle, test send into Mailpit, script draft refused on publish, invalid brand import rejected, brand save persists across reload
why: prove the UI on the real stack, not by reading code

decision: reworded two early rows and moved two rows about the first host app's internals to that app's private pull request
why: this repo is public and client-neutral; the UI agent spotted the client name in the log

decision: the admin UI was built by a subagent in its own worktree from the approved prototype; reviewed its screenshots and checked every server action and page requires an admin session
why: own the delegate's work: inspect artifacts, not its summary
evidence: commit f086b4f; /tmp/mailflow-ui/*.png; grep requireAdmin in src/app/(admin)

decision: Docker image runs migrations then the server; a fresh database installs the example workflow as draft so nothing sends until an admin sets it live
why: safe first boot for every new deployment
evidence: docker run smoke: health ok, /workflows redirects to /signed-out, failed-payment status draft

decision: removed the notify and end step kinds and the unsubscribe-is-an-error rule from the docs
why: the docs promised things the code does not do

decision: a real browser walk found admin sign-in broken: the redirect after /sso used the host Next thinks it has, so the browser landed on a different host without the session cookie; now a relative Location
why: same bug would bite behind any proxy in production; found by walking the real flow across both apps
evidence: src/app/sso/route.ts, tests/sso.test.ts; walk: click Mail lands on /workflows signed in

decision: closed an open redirect in the sign-in next parameter and set the cookie Secure from x-forwarded-proto
why: spotted while fixing the redirect; //host would have sent an admin to another site

decision: host app to mailflow end to end: a Stripe-signed payment_failed webhook into the host app started a run and the first email reached Mailpit; the replay was deduplicated; invoice.paid stopped the run; a live signed check reached the host's invoice lookup
why: prove the integration on real processes, not only shared test vectors
